text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein and Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister Prince Saud al-Feisal discuss the peace process; they review bilateral ties and latest regional and international issues.
- King heads next week to Britain, France, Switzerland and Holland as part of a European tour.
- Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali says Jordanian economy attains progress in every field.
- Deputy Prime Minister Abdullah Ensour says government has no intention to postphone November parliamentary elections.
- Jordan's largest Islamist opposition party, the Islamic Action Front (IAF), begins process of selecting candidates in some districts at the start of plans for November elections.
- Crown Prince Hassan calls for laying the foundations for Islamic-Christian co-existence.
- Doctors Union, in a step to ease tensions with the government, says it is ready to enter into talks over its pay demands.
- Government plans to restructure eight services ministries by merging some of them such as the ministry of youth with culture, and higher education with education.
- King attends a joint live military exercise by Jordanian and U.S. troops in the desert; part of routine joint military exercises.
- Private sector allowed to export surplus olive oil.
- Crown Prince calls for implementing a free-trade accord with Bahrain.
